herald.label: Comic Book Herald · reading order and collection contents

order.label: Comic Book Reading Orders · issue chronology

hickman.label: Penguin Random House · Hickman collection and recognition

stories.title: The origin & the Lee/Ditko beginning
stories.why: The original foundation. Choose this if you enjoy classic comics and want to meet Peter and his world from the beginning.
stories.match: Both collections include the origin and the first ten Amazing Spider-Man issues; choose either edition.

stories.title: If This Be My Destiny… / Master Planner
stories.why: An early test of Peter’s resolve; a recurring critics’ pick.
stories.match: Masterworks Vol. 4 covers #31–40, including this story.

stories.title: Green Goblin unmasked
stories.why: A major step in Peter’s long conflict with the Green Goblin.
stories.match: Also in Masterworks Vol. 4. Do not borrow it twice if you already read #31–40.

stories.title: Spider-Man No More!
stories.why: A defining look at the personal cost of being Spider-Man.
stories.match: Masterworks Vol. 5 covers #41–50.

stories.title: The Death of Captain Stacy
stories.why: A key supporting-cast turning point.
stories.match: The Epic Collection covers #86–104.

stories.title: The Night Gwen Stacy Died
stories.why: A major milestone. Read before Blue, which reflects on Peter’s earlier relationships.
stories.match: No confirmed collection match in the supplied catalog. Man-Wolf at Midnight starts at #124 and does not fill this gap.

stories.title: Nothing Can Stop the Juggernaut
stories.why: A short classic and a good taste of Roger Stern’s Spider-Man.
stories.match: Choose the dedicated collection or the larger Epic Collection. Both include the core story.

stories.title: Origin of the Hobgoblin
stories.why: The opening Hobgoblin mystery; continue here if you like Stern’s run.
stories.match: Use the dedicated Origin collection. The Juggernaut Epic ends at #241 and only overlaps the beginning.

stories.title: The Kid Who Collects Spider-Man
stories.why: A small, character-focused story often singled out by readers.
stories.match: No confirmed match. The Juggernaut Epic’s #224–241 range does not reach this issue.

stories.title: The Death of Jean DeWolff
stories.why: A darker street-level story, best after meeting Peter’s world.
stories.match: No confirmed collection match in the supplied catalog.

stories.title: Kraven’s Last Hunt
stories.issues: Web of Spider-Man #31 → Amazing Spider-Man #293 → Spectacular Spider-Man #131 → Web #32 → Amazing #294 → Spectacular #132
stories.why: A frequently recommended dark classic. Some familiarity with Peter and Mary Jane helps.
stories.match: Choose Marvel Select or the larger Epic Collection; both contain the six-part story.

stories.title: Venom’s debut & early confrontations
stories.why: A key villain introduction, with earlier black-suit background in the same collection.
stories.match: Birth of Venom contains earlier material too. It overlaps the black-costume era; this entry is placed at Venom’s debut.

stories.title: Ultimate Spider-Man: Power & Responsibility
stories.why: The clearest modern teenage-Peter entry point in this guide. A separate continuity begins here.
stories.match: Continue with Vol. 2: Learning Curve (#8–13), then Vol. 3: Double Trouble (#14–21); both are also in your catalog.

stories.title: Coming Home & The Conversation
stories.why: A widely recommended modern entry into the established adult Peter’s life.
stories.match: Modern Era Epic: Coming Home contains #30–45, including #38. This is the 1999 series, not the 1963 numbering.

stories.title: Spider-Man: Blue
stories.why: A reflective relationship story. Published here, but looks back at Peter’s early years; read after the Gwen milestone.
stories.match: No confirmed collection match in the supplied catalog.

stories.title: Marvel Knights Spider-Man by Mark Millar
stories.why: A contained twelve-issue adventure for readers who already know the basic cast.
stories.match: Collected as Spider-Man By Mark Millar Ultimate Collection. ‘Ultimate Collection’ is an edition label; this is main-universe Peter.

stories.title: Brand New Day
stories.why: A fresh status quo and another practical jumping-on point, though the reset behind it is divisive.
stories.match: Choose Vol. 1 or Complete Collection Vol. 1; the larger collection continues further. These are alternatives.

stories.title: Big Time
stories.why: A useful entry into Dan Slott’s era before Spider-Island.
stories.match: Modern Era Epic: Big Time is matched by exact catalog ISBN and collection title.

stories.title: Ultimate: Death of Spider-Man
stories.why: A major endpoint for Bendis’s Peter. Save it until after the earlier Ultimate volumes.
stories.match: This is Vol. 4: Death of Spider-Man, not the Avengers vs. New Ultimates companion.

stories.title: Spider-Island
stories.why: A major Slott-era event; follows Big Time.
stories.match: The dedicated collection lists the core Amazing Spider-Man issues. This guide does not require every crossover tie-in.

stories.title: Superior Spider-Man — the original run
stories.issues: Superior Spider-Man (2013) #1–31; preceded by Amazing Spider-Man #698–700
stories.why: A major change in who wears the mask; read the setup first.
stories.match: No confirmed original-run collection match. Supernova and Superior Spider-Man Returns are later material and are not substitutes.

stories.title: Spider-Verse
stories.why: The big multiverse crossover. Easier once you have a feel for Peter’s solo stories.
stories.match: Vol. 3: Spider-Verse contains the core Amazing issues; it is not every tie-in. Vol. 2: Spider-Verse Prelude is also in the catalog.

stories.title: Spider-Man: Life Story
stories.why: A lifetime of Spider-Man reimagined. Best as a later perspective on the milestones above.
stories.match: The six-issue collection is in your catalog. It is a separate retelling, not the next chapter of main continuity.

stories.title: Ultimate Spider-Man: Married With Children
stories.why: A fresh adult-Peter starting point, featuring a married Peter with children.
stories.match: Hickman’s Vol. 1. Separate from Bendis’s 2000 Ultimate series; you do not need to read that run first.
